correctness.rationale: Both source hazards have the common form x^(alpha-1)R0(x)/m_alpha(x). Half-normal and Maxwell survivals have Gaussian tails with polynomial powers -1 and +1 respectively. L'Hospital's rule applied to m_alpha(x) and beta^2 x^(alpha-2) R0(x) gives their ratio tending to one, hence h_alpha(x)~x/beta^2. The lower-endpoint formula follows from the tail-integral identity for the alpha-th baseline moment. The packaged checker independently evaluates the exact integral formulas and the numerical examples.

value.rationale: Hazard-shape flexibility is presented as a reliability feature of both newly introduced special cases. The theorem removes the globally decreasing class for the entire positive parameter space and proves an unavoidable interior minimum whenever alpha is below one. This changes the structural reliability interpretation of both models and explains why a finite-window decline cannot be extrapolated to the whole support.
